newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU Commission tackles Italy, France over VAT rules.
newsitem.headline: EU Commission tackles Italy, France over VAT rules.

text.p: The European Commission said on Thursday it had taken Italy and France to the European Court of justice for failing to respect EU-wide VAT rules and warned Greece it faced the same fate for fixing the price of tobacco.
Italy was blamed for preventing self-employed people from deducting Value Added Tax paid when buying a house if the acquisition was made jointly with a non-taxable person, such as a husband and wife.
France was found to infringe separate 1979 rules on the refund of VAT when a company subcontracts part of its work to another firm in a separate EU state.

The Commission also criticised the French tax authorities for exempting samples worth less than 200 francs from VAT, saying EU rules provided for no maximum value. A Commission official said this discriminated against samples of art books.
In this case, however, the Commission sent France a reasoned opinion -- the last step before Court action.
In another statement, the Commission said it had sent Greece two reasoned opinions regarding VAT collected on taxi firms and the practice of fixing the price of manufactured tobacco.
The first Greek infringement was to collect a flat amount of VAT on taxi businesses, which the Commission said was lower than it should be.
Secondly, it contested the fixing by the Greek Finance Ministry of a minimum price for tobacco, saying that the price should be determined by the manufacturers or importers.
